event.title: Fedra Yazdi: Notes on a Non-Arrival

event.title: Anne McKee Fund: Fine Art Auction
event.excerpt: A Key West tradition where art and generosity meet. Take home a new favorite work of Florida Keys artwork, and support our creative community, with proceeds benefiting both participating artists and the Anne McKee Artists Fund.

event.title: Lothar Speer: Documenting Conflict
event.excerpt: Speer’s original courtroom drawings from the federal trial and sentencing of Ryan Wesley Routh offer an immediate visual record of gesture, expression and atmosphere, and a rare look at how an artist documents history as it happens.

event.title: Rita Troxel and Fred Troxel: Earth and Bone
event.excerpt: Ceramic sculptures and found-object assemblages unite clay, bone, and metal in an exploration of impermanence. Inspired by nature’s cycles, each work balances vulnerability and strength, inviting reflection on memory and transformation.

event.title: With The Grain II: Stories in Wood
event.excerpt: From miniature worlds to imaginary beings, these woodworks are cut, carved, chiseled and assembled, invariably retaining the warmth and character of the medium.

event.title: Charles Spitzack: Cut Against the Grain
event.excerpt: Seattle artist Charles Spitzack celebrates the joy of the handmade, with woodcut prints and custom frames that delight in architecture and ornamentation he’s observed during artist residencies in Key West and elsewhere.

event.title: Hue Cares: Every Color Has a Cause
event.excerpt: Inspired by the unmistakable colors of Key West—from conch houses and coral reefs to bougainvillea and brilliant sunsets—local artists interpret the island’s vibrant palette in works across a range of media.

event.title: Samuel Alvarez: The World Here
event.excerpt: A master of contemporary realism, Alvarez gives familiar Key West scenes a heightened sense of scale and presence, treating the lush vegetation of the Keys not as backdrop, but as a living force.

event.title: Yvette Esquinaldo Lee: I’ll Hand You My Keys
event.excerpt: Lee uses the traditional Key West medium of bas-relief wood carvings to reflect on growing up on the island. Her subject matter is centered on the flora, fauna and people whose spirits she highlights in bold, colorful renderings.

event.title: Bright Minds: A Schools @ The Studios Exhibition
event.excerpt: Each school year, more than a thousand school kids visit The Studios’ galleries through our flagship education program, talking directly to artists and then making work of their own.

event.title: Bex McCharen: How the Water Remembers Us
event.excerpt: Combining video, holographics, textile, and installation, Bex McCharen draws visitors into South Florida waterways as spaces of memory, transformation, and collective care.

event.title: Nya Patrinos: Crossed and Entangled Waters
event.excerpt: Through the intersecting Key West histories of ten ships, Patrinos traces slavery’s entangled centuries: illegal voyages; confinement; deadly deportations, and the wrecked Henrietta Marie.

event.title: Megan Hildebrandt: Rich and Fractured
event.excerpt: By turns emotionally raw and comically absurd, Hildebrandt blurs boundaries between mother, artist and self through drawings and animation.

event.title: Turner Harrison: Beyond the Yetiverse
event.excerpt: Blast off into the sprawling, multimedia universe of Key West psychedelic rock band AstroYeti through sketches, concept art and over 400 trading card designs created by the band’s frontman and multi-instrumentalist.

event.title: Evan Gershkovich
event.description:
In March 2023, a year after Russia invaded Ukraine, Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich met with a source in an empty restaurant 900 miles east of Moscow. Masked agents charged in, blindfolded Gershkovich, and dragged him into an unmarked van. The agents were from the FSB, Putin’s security service, and the successor to the Soviet-era KGB. Five years earlier, Gershkovich—whose parents had left the Soviet Union in the 1970s for New Jersey—arrived in Moscow to start his journalism career.

Interrogated for hours after his arrest, Gershkovich was charged with spying and thrown in Moscow’s notorious Lefortovo prison—a pawn in a geopolitical chess match. After his world shrunk to a tiny cell, Gershkovich continued reporting. For the next sixteen months, he documented a life in Russia that few Westerners will ever experience: its sprawling prison system, with its own vocabulary and customs—and surprising pockets of humanity.

In This Cursed Beautiful Land: A Russian-American Story, Gershkovich recounts the events leading to his arrest, his nearly 500 days in Russian prisons, and the multi-country prisoner swap that freed him. More than a prison memoir, it’s a chronicle of a misunderstood people and their land.

Gershkovich will be in conversation with Peter Baker, the chief White House correspondent for The New York Times.

This event will be ASL-interpreted. To sit in the interpreted section or to access the interpreted feed virtually, contact Amanda.
event.excerpt: In This Cursed Beautiful Land: A Russian-American Story, the Wall Street Journal reporter who was wrongly imprisoned in Russia for more than a year recounts the events leading to his arrest, his nearly 500 days in Russian prisons, and the multi-country prisoner swap that freed him.

event.title: Dancin’ in the Streets: A Simchat Torah Celebration
event.description:
6:00 pm: Class with Rabbi Jenna
6:30 pm: Happy Hour
7:30 pm: Service and dancing

Simchat Torah, which means “Rejoicing in Torah,” is the day when we gather to renew ourselves as we begin the cycle of reading from Genesis once again. Let loose and dance like no one’s watching as you enjoy live music, themed cocktails and mocktails, and lively dancing on I Street.

Before the main event, choose from taking a class with Rabbi Jenna diving into the holiday and exploring the first few lines of the Torah, or get social and meet new people at our happy hour.

Class: Make it Make Sense

On Simchat Torah, we read the very first lines of Torah and the story of creation – not making something out of nothing but rather creating order out of chaos – tohu va-vohu. In a world that at times feels too chaotic to comprehend, how can we continue to create meaningful and joyful experiences? Explore these big questions and more through a text study with Rabbi Jenna.

Must be 21+ and present ID to attend. No one will be turned away from any of our programs due to lack of funds. For more information, please contact our Director of Jewish Life,  Nathan.

event.title: John Grisham
event.description:
In The French Illusion, John Grisham—the author of more than fifty consecutive #1 New York Times bestsellers—delivers a gripping page-turner about a honeymoon gone horribly wrong and the nightmare that follows. After Paul and Chelsea Tanner’s fairytale wedding, their future is full of promise. But their honeymoon to Paris takes a dark, shocking turn when they are kidnapped while on a day trip to the French countryside. Who would target them, and why?

The search for clues stretches across borders, with the FBI, CIA, and French Intelligence working to put the pieces of the puzzle together. Struggling to find answers, a young lawyer is recruited to be the bait in an elaborate CIA operation. Propulsive and surprising, The French Illusion is an unmistakable Grisham thrill ride.

Grisham’s recent books include Framed, Camino Ghosts, and The Exchange: After the Firm. He has been honored with the Library of Congress Creative Achievement Award for Fiction.

Grisham will be in conversation with David Baldacci, a #1 New York Times bestselling author of more than fifty thriller and crime novels and seven YA novels. Baldacci is also the cofounder, along with his wife, of the Wish You Well Foundation, a nonprofit dedicated to supporting literacy efforts across the U.S.

event.title: Michael Douglas
event.description:
From his fractured childhood through recounting his career through twelve of his most iconic films, Academy Award, Golden Globe, and Emmy Award-winning actor and producer Michael Douglas finally gives the full and uncensored account of his life in One Helluva Ride.

Initially dismissed as just the handsome son of legendary movie star Kirk Douglas, at age thirty-one Douglas surprised Hollywood when he won his first Oscar for producing One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest. Told he would never be more than a TV actor, he quit the hit series “The Streets of San Francisco” and went on to win a second Oscar for his performance in Wall Street.

Yet as Douglas’s fame grew, so did his personal struggles: his turbulent first mar­riage; infidelity and affairs; his struggle with alcohol, drugs and rehab; the fight to save his son from an addiction that sent him to prison; and his battle with stage IV cancer. He saw Catherine Zeta Jones on a movie screen and instantly fell for her. Their incredible love story transformed his life, enduring after twenty-five years of marriage.

Douglas will be in conversation with Kelly Corrigan, the author of four New York Times bestselling memoirs about family life as well as two children’s books. She hosts the podcast, “Kelly Corrigan Wonders,” and the show “Tell Me More” on PBS.

event.title: Yotam Ottolenghi
event.description:
Eight years after redefining “flavor without fuss,” Yotam Ottolenghi—one of the most influential voices in contemporary food—offers Simple Too, the follow-up to his bestselling cookbook, Ottolenghi Simple. In a world of endless notifications, Ottolenghi explores what “simple” means now and why bold flavor remains at the heart of simplicity. In conversation, he’ll share recipes that work with you, not against you, and dishes you can begin with half a plan and still end with a deeply satisfying meal.

Ottolenghi will dive into the ingredients and techniques that shape this new collection: beans simply dressed, black chickpeas, sesame in generous handfuls, sweet-and-spicy balances, pasta cooked directly in its sauce, and whole meals roasted in a single tray. He’ll also introduce the “Fundamentals” chapter—fifteen fridge-ready flavor builders like spring onion oil, green salsa, za’atar oil, confit tomatoes, and chilli crisp—small things that make big differences on busy weeknights. Simple Too is less about doing less and more about making everyday cooking feel generous, achievable, and full of joy.

Renowned for his vegetable-forward cuisine and imaginative approach to everyday cooking, Ottolenghi’s acclaimed cookbooks include Plenty, Jerusalem, Simple, Flavor, and Sweet. His work extends to successful delis and restaurants, where bold combinations, fresh produce, and multicultural inspirations meet. Ottolenghi will be in conversation with Carla Hall, a chef, co-host of the YouTube show “Chewed Up,” former co-host of the Emmy Award-winning TV show “The Chew,” and the author most recently of Carla Bakes: Sweet, Savory, and from the Heart.

This service will be ASL-interpreted. To sit in the interpreted section or to access the interpreted feed virtually, contact Amanda.
event.excerpt: In a world of endless notifications, Ottolenghi—one of the most influential voices in contemporary food—explores what “simple” means now and why bold flavor remains at the heart of simplicity in Simple Too.

event.description:
Listen to Chelsea Wolfe

Acclaimed musician, songwriter, and multidisciplinary artist Chelsea Wolfe returns with new music at the center of a world that she is only beginning to reveal. “The Dark” and “Death is Not the End” arrive after a week of fan speculation, sparked by cryptic imagery, fragments of sound, and the shadowy visual language teased by Heretic Parfum across its socials.

Wolfe has become one of the most singular artists in the world, moving fluidly between doom metal, folk, industrial, electronic music, and spectral balladry. She has collaborated with artists including Deftones’ Chino Moreno, Xiu Xiu, and Converge, had her music featured in HBO’s “Game of Thrones,” co-wrote the score for the A24 horror film X with Tyler Bates, and turned heads at last year’s Ann Demeulemeester show at Paris Fashion Week.

Known for building immersive worlds where darkness and beauty are indistinguishable, Wolfe has cultivated a devoted global following through music that explores transformation, spirituality, grief, longing, and the unseen forces that shape our lives. With these new songs and GHOSTS arriving in close succession, she opens the door to a new chapter that feels unmistakably her own.

Josh Thomas burst onto the Australian comedy scene when he became the youngest ever winner of Raw Comedy, the prestigious national competition produced by the Melbourne Comedy Festival. Two years later, while still in his teens, he received a Melbourne Comedy Festival nomination for Best Show.

Thomas is best known for writing, acting, and co-executive producing his own TV show, “Please Like Me,” inspired by his life, which was named one of the best TV shows of the year by Entertainment Weekly, The New Yorker, and Time. His writing for the show won awards from the Australian Academy (AACTA) and the Australian Writers Guild. The show won Best Comedy at the AACTA Awards, Most Outstanding Comedy at the Logie Awards, and was nominated as Best Comedy at the International Emmy Awards, Rose d’Or Awards, and GLAAD Media Awards. Thomas also created and starred in the TV show, “Everything’s Gonna Be Okay.” He recently launched a weekly podcast, “Josh Thomas and Friends and You,” featuring conversations with his friends.

event.title: Simone Dinnerstein, piano
event.description:
Listen to Simone Dinnerstein

Lauded by The Washington Post as “an artist of strikingly original ideas and irrefutable integrity,” Simone Dinnerstein returns for an evening of distinctive artistry. The program opens with Rameau’s rarely performed Gavotte et six doubles, followed by American composer Philip Lasser’s Twelve Variations on Chorale by J.S. Bach, exploring the power and modernity of Bach’s harmonic poetry. Dinnerstein continues to demonstrate her “unique voice in the forest of Bach interpretation” (The New York Times) with the composer’s 15 Sinfonias, and closes her program with Keith Jarrett’s Encore from “Tokyo,” ending the night on a note of otherworldly serenity. 

Dinnerstein’s performance is the fifth-annual Ruth Bader Ginsburg Memorial Recital—a creative initiative connecting Justice Ginsburg’s love of music, the esteemed artists she championed and befriended, and the future of the vocal and instrumental arts in which she delighted. 

Program:
Rameau – Gavotte et six doubles
Lasser – Twelve Variations on Chorale by J.S. Bach
Bach – 15 Sinfonias, BWV 787-801
Jarrett / trans. Uwe Karcher – Encore from “Tokyo” 

Photo by Lisa-Marie Mazzucco

event.title: How to be a Jewish Adult
event.description:
This 8-week workshop meets Tuesdays starting October 20, with some exceptions. The full dates are Tuesdays, October 20, 27, November 3, 10, 17, December 1, 8, and 15 from 6:30 – 8:30 pm.

Do you ever feel like you could use a handbook for how to build a Jewish life? If you identify as Jewish or Jew-ish but aren’t sure how to incorporate Judaism into your day-to-day life, this 8-week series offers equal parts community-building and deep-dive into core lessons from our tradition to help you feel more Jewishly connected. 

Led by Rabbi Loren Berman, each class will take on an essential Jewish value or teaching including big topics ranging from love and relationships, social justice, unpacking what it means to be spiritual, and more. In a judgement-free space, you’ll consider how to apply these teachings to your life in a way that feels personal, meaningful, and authentic to you as you build community with others in their 20s and 30s who are curious to engage with Judaism in practical and profound ways.

About Rabbi Loren Berman
Guest Rabbi Loren Berman has taught and mentored at Sixth & I since moving to DC in 2023. Currently a full-time consultant in the public sector, he previously worked with Jews in their 20s and 30s at Sefaria and Moishe House.

No one will be turned away from any of our classes due to lack of funds. For more information, please contact our Jewish Life Associate, Robyn.

event.description:
Listen to Niladri Kumaar

Niladri Kumaar, sitar
Agnelo Fernandes, keys
Sambit Chatterjee, drums
Satyajit Talwalkar, tabla 

Celebrated sitar maestro Niladri Kumaar is a compelling force in Indian classical music and an innovator who carries centuries of tradition in every note. This evening is both a forward-looking showcase and a tribute to an irreplaceable musical bond: curated selections from Space Between the Notes, the only recorded live performance between Kumaar and the late, legendary Zakir Hussain. Their singular partnership resounds once more—a gift, before the album’s release later this year.

Featuring sitar, zitar, and an ensemble of Indian and American musicians with jazz influences, this is Indian music at its most expansive, where centuries of classical tradition meet improvisational spirit.

event.title: Making Meaning in the Modern World
event.description:
Our well-being grows when we create, when we connect, and when we know that we matter to other people. Decades of research and thousands of human stories tell us that making and mattering are powerful antidotes to overwhelm and disconnection.

Join New York Times bestselling authors Kelly Corrigan (The Middle Place and Tell Me More) and Jennifer Wallace (Never Enough and Mattering) for a conversation about making, mattering, and the simple things that help us build meaningful lives. Drawing from Corrigan’s exploration of creativity and making, and Wallace’s analysis and collection of research on the science of mattering, the evening weaves together personal stories and practical wisdom to explore what helps people flourish. The event features individual talks from each author and an on-stage conversation between the authors and local educators.

Come celebrate the simple but powerful idea that the lives we build together are shaped by both what we make and by knowing that we matter.

This event is supported by the Walton Family Foundation.

event.title: Sophia Bush
event.description:
Sophia Bush has always understood the power of stories. She’s seen it in the connection millions of viewers have had to the women she’s played on-screen—Dr. Sam Griffith on “Good Sam” and Dr. Cass Beckman on “Grey’s Anatomy,” Detective Erin Lindsay on “Chicago P.D.,” and the iconic Brooke Davis on “One Tree Hill.” She’s seen it in her activism, where speaking truth to inequality and power has prompted real change. And she’s seen it in her personal life, when her experiences and opinions have been distorted to drive clicks and create drama.

In And I Will Tell You Mine, Bush shares stories about what has most shaped her: her childhood in Los Angeles, the unexpected road from journalism student to actor, navigating Hollywood and fighting for her character’s integrity, and the realities of marriage and divorce. She also offers sides of herself not often seen: the lifelong learner, the friend, the adventurer. And I Will Tell You Mine is an account of becoming, un-becoming, and becoming again to return home to our truest selves.

Bush will be in conversation with Aaron Parnas, an independent journalist, political commentator, and attorney.

This service will be ASL-interpreted. To sit in the interpreted section or to access the interpreted feed virtually, contact Amanda.

event.title: Rick Steves
event.description:
In the 1970s, the ultimate trip for any backpacker was the storied “Hippie Trail,” a 3,000-mile trek from Istanbul to Kathmandu. A 23-year-old Rick Steves made the trek in 1978, and like a travel writer in training, he documented everything along the way: jumping off a moving train, making friends in Tehran, getting lost in Lahore, getting high for the first time in Herat, battling leeches in Pokhara, and more. The experience ignited his love of travel and forever broadened his perspective on the world.

On the Hippie Trail: Istanbul to Kathmandu and the Making of a Travel Writer—a New York Times bestseller now out in paperback—contains edited selections from Rick Steves’ journal and travel photos with a 45-years-later preface and postscript reflecting on how his journey through Turkey, Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, and Nepal changed his life.

event.title: LeVar Burton
event.description:
Tracing the different eras of his life—from “Roots” to “Star Trek: The Next Generation” to “Reading Rainbow” and far beyond the camera—actor LeVar Burton fearlessly opens up about growing up during the Civil Rights Movement, being raised by a remarkable mother, and discovering his calling as a storyteller in Take My Word for It. He explores how acting has served as both a source of transformation and an escape from the most difficult parts of his past, while also confronting the challenges of being a parent, husband, and householder.

As Burton honors the loved ones whose strength and resilience shaped him, he also asks what we owe to our ancestors and to each other, reflecting on the deep necessity he’s always felt to advocate for liberation and equity.

event.title: Yung Pueblo
event.description:
Journey: The Year That Changes Everything is a year-long guide to awareness, reflection, and personal growth from #1 New York Times bestselling author, Time 100 Creator, meditator, and modern poet, Yung Pueblo.

Healing is not a destination: it’s a practice. The greatest change comes from within you. To transform your life, you must go on an inward journey to uncover two of the greatest prizes a human being can have: self-awareness and inner peace. Both emerge from a deep state of balance, expressed in the visible world by the four major elements:

Fire – the element of ambition, transformation, energy, and understanding boundaries – helps you work through the anxiousness and uncertainty that come up as you steel yourself for change.
Air – the element of motion, freedom, self-awareness, and skillfulness – guides you as you move forward and take flight.
Earth – the element of stability, self-care, steadiness, and nourishment – is all about training. You need to continue the work so change can be lasting.
Water – the element of letting go, generosity, and adaptability – is about feeling balance and being in a place to unlock new opportunities, relationships, and a new understanding of yourself.

event.description:
Listen to Minsoo Sohn

“A genuine artist, with a thoughtfully conceived and poetic interpretation.” – The New York Times

Pianist Minsoo Sohn debuts with Washington Performing Arts for a program exhibiting his undeniable musical intelligence and masterful virtuosity. Studied by the likes of Beethoven and Mozart, Bach’s The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I, is frequently regarded as one of the most significant works in the history of classical music. Sohn brings his own poetic interpretation to this storied collection of 24 prelude and fugue pairs, creating an unforgettable evening with one of the most audacious and influential works for piano as the centerpiece.

Known for his career as a devoted pedagogue, Sohn is also recognized as the teacher of Yunchan Lim, the youngest first-prize winner in the history of the Van Cliburn International Piano Competition.

event.title: Susan Spungen: Talk & Tasting
event.description:
All hail the Cookie Queen! Dubbed by The New York Times as the “Babe Ruth of Cookies,” Susan Spungen—a cook, food stylist, recipe developer, cookbook author, and Founding Food Editor at Martha Stewart Living—shows how making cookies is both an art and a craft in Cookie Queen: 80+ Irresistible, Doable, Giftable Recipes.

Equal parts technical masterclass and love letter to the cookie, Cookie Queen draws from global traditions and bold flavor combinations for sweet and salty recipes to satisfy a simple cookie fix or to make cookie gift boxes. Spungen covers essential equipment and a well-stocked cookie pantry, best practices and tricks, plus guidance on decorating.

For a delicious take on show-and-tell, add a 3-cookie-pack to your ticket order to try recipes from the book (made by Capitol Jill Baking) that Spungen will discuss during the talk while you savor these treats: halvah mandelbrot, jammy sandies, and cardamom black pepper cookies (recipes contain nuts).

Spungen is the author of Recipes: A Collection for the Modern Cook and What’s a Hostess to Do? among other cookbooks. She was the culinary consultant on films including Julie & Julia and Eat, Pray, Love. Spungen will be in conversation with Claudia Fleming, a James Beard award-winning pastry chef, executive pastry director at Union Square Hospitality Group, and the author of Delectable: Sweet & Savory Baking.

A book signing will follow the event for those who would like their name added to their book.

event.title: Aga Khan Master Musicians
event.description:
Listen to the Aga Khan Master Musicians

Aga Khan Master Musicians
Basel Rajoub, saxophone and clarinet
Feras Charestan, qanun
Yurdal Tokcan, oud
Abbos Kosimov, drum
Vincent Peirani, accordion

Washington Performing Arts presents an evening where the musical worlds of Central Asia, China, the Middle East, and contemporary Europe meet in striking and unexpected harmony. Five performers from the Aga Khan Master Musicians—an artistic collective dedicated to living musical traditions—are joined by celebrated French artist Vincent Peirani for a concert that is wholly its own.

Syrian-born Basel Rajoub has reimagined an entirely new vocabulary for the saxophone; his compatriot Feras Charestan commands the qanun, the shimmering Middle Eastern plucked zither. Turkish oud master Yurdal Tokcan and Uzbek percussionist Abbos Kosimov, a virtuoso on the doira frame drum, complete the collective’s lineup. They are joined by Vincent Peirani, award-winning accordionist, singer, and composer whose work spans jazz, contemporary music, and improvisation. Six distinct voices in one extraordinary evening.

Photos courtesy of AKMP, Sebastian Schutyser, and Stan Augris

event.title: Rebekah Lowin: Talk & Workshop
event.description:
Part cookbook, part entertaining toolkit, and part joyful Jewish field guide, A Year of Jewish Joy blends ancient traditions with modern charm to help you bring beauty, warmth, and creativity to Shabbat and the major Jewish holidays. Author Rebekah Lowin—affectionately dubbed a “Jewish Martha Stewart” by her readers—guides you through the traditions, blessings, and rituals that anchor Jewish life. Along the way, she shares menu ideas—including 75 recipes—plus entertaining tips, handmade details, and table inspirations.

From Rosh Hashanah to Tu B’Av, A Year of Jewish Joy turns the calendar into a year of fresh and accessible celebrations worth showing up for—hungry. For example:

  • Welcome Rosh Hashanah with Caramelized Onion Holiday Brisket, Hawaij-Spiced Apple Galette, and individual “honey flights.”
  • Kick off Hanukkah with Gelt Wrapper Flowers, Caviar-Topped Party Latkes, Brigadeiro Sufganiyot, and Olive Oil Martinis.

Lowin is a writer and content creator known for her whimsical, design-forward approach to Jewish holiday cooking, décor, craft projects, and storytelling. She will be in conversation with Rabbi Jenna Shaw of Sixth & I.

Sprinkle Embroidery Cake Decorating Workshop: From 4:00 – 5:30 pm (before the 6:00 pm event), join Rebekah for a hands-on take on the viral sprinkle embroidery cake trend. You’ll create an intricate, stitch-inspired design on your own individual mini sheet cake to take home. She’ll share instructions and plenty of design inspiration, or you can dream up something entirely your own. Bring a friend and come decorate with us! All supplies will be provided. Decorations will be certified kosher. Kosher cakes available upon request.

Led by Rabbi Loren Berman, each class will take on an essential Jewish value or teaching including big topics ranging from love and relationships, social justice, unpacking what it means to be spiritual, and more. In a judgement-free space, you’ll consider how to apply these teachings to your life in a way that feels personal, meaningful, and authentic to you as you build community with others in their 20s and 30s who are curious to engage with Judaism in practical and profound ways.

About Rabbi Loren Berman
Guest Rabbi Loren Berman has taught and mentored at Sixth & I since moving to DC in 2023. Currently a full-time consultant in the public sector, he previously worked with Jews in their 20s and 30s at Sefaria and Moishe House.

No one will be turned away from any of our classes due to lack of funds. For more information, please contact our Jewish Life Associate, Robyn.

Following the release of her acclaimed debut I Need to Start a Garden and its long-awaited follow-up Seed of a Seed, Haley Heynderickx recently released What of Our Nature, a collaboration with Max García Conover. After a year of touring with Garcia and working on new material, she now returns to the road for a rare run of solo performances.

One of contemporary folk’s most quietly captivating voices, Heynderickx writes with warmth, wit, and self-reflection. Her songs find wonder in the everyday while exploring questions of identity, belonging, and our relationship with the natural world. Tender, thoughtful and quietly spellbinding, these shows are an invitation to step into the unknown with her and leave a little room for what may come next.

event.title: Seth Parker Woods, cello, and Conor Hanick, piano
event.description:
Listen to Seth Parker Woods
Listen to Conor Hanick

Cellist Seth Parker Woods and pianist Conor Hanick unite for an evening of commanding musicianship at the intersection of tradition and discovery. A three-time GRAMMY nominee, Woods has garnered a reputation for versatile and inventive musicality, and is joined by pianist Hanick, praised for his precision with classic and contemporary fare.

Their program brings together Fazil Say’s vivid Four Cities, George Walker’s 1956 Sonata for cello and piano—of which Gramophone writes that Woods and Hanick’s recording is “more compellingly characterful,” with “the raw vulnerability of the central slow movement” lingering in the memory — and Rachmaninoff’s sweeping Cello Sonata, op. 19, one of the most passionate works in the duo repertoire.

Program:
Fazil Say – Four Cities
George Walker – Sonata for cello and piano (1956)
Sergei Rachmaninoff – Cello Sonata, op. 19 

Photos courtesy of Ben Gibbs and Rob Davidson

event.title: Balourdet Quartet
event.description:
Listen to the Balourdet Quartet

Recipient of the 2024 Avery Fisher Career Grant and Chamber Music America’s Cleveland Quartet Award, the Balourdet Quartet was born from late-night chamber music sessions and became one of the most celebrated young ensembles in the world. Described as “unafraid to show its personality,” their playing balances clarity with expressive warmth, and a deep belief that music exists to break down walls. Their Washington Performing Arts program reflects that ambition: spanning four centuries from Monteverdi to Ben Johnston’s microtonal meditation on “Amazing Grace,” with Bartók’s haunted and personal Sixth Quartet, and Mendelssohn’s passionately constructed Second at the center. 

Program:
Claudio Monteverdi (arr. Benjamin Zannoni) – Selection of Madrigals
Béla Bartók – String Quartet No. 6, Sz. 85
Ben Johnston – String Quartet No. 4, “Amazing Grace”
Felix Mendelssohn – String Quartet No. 2 in A Minor, op. 13 

Photo by Luke Ratray

event.title: Anthony “Tony” Walker & Friends
event.description:
Listen to Anthony “Tony” Walker

Washington, DC, has given the music world some of the most transcendent voices in American music. Longtime Washington Performing Arts Children of the Gospel Choir music director and accompanist, producer, educator, and DMV-area luminary Anthony “Tony” Walker leads an evening celebrating the legendary Roberta Flack, Marvin Gaye, Donnie Hathaway, and Richard Smallwood, whose roots in DC’s Black communities helped shape the sound of a nation. Part concert, part storytelling, the evening weaves the music and the stories together to celebrate the people and places behind the songs you know by heart.

Photo by Ashera J Photography

event.title: Paul Huang, violin
event.description:
Listen to Paul Huang

Four acclaimed musicians join together in a powerful program meditating on time, loss, and hope. Bela Kovacs’ Sholem Alekhem, rov Feidman! is a vibrant clarinet homage to klezmer song and spirit, laughter edged with lament. It casts light on the echoes that follow, reminding us that even in the face of ruin, sound endures. Shostakovich’s Piano Trio No. 2, written amid war and loss, spins a ghostly klezmer dance: ironic, grief-stricken, unforgiving. Messiaen’s Quartet for the End of Time, born in a prison camp, reaches beyond suffering toward eternity, where time dissolves into silence and praise. These works are fragments of memory, breath, and belief; resonating through the stillness that time leaves behind.

Program:
Dmitri Shostakovich – Piano Trio No. 2 in E Minor
Bela Kovacs – Sholem-Alekhem, rov Feidman!
Olivier Messiaen – Quartet for the End of Time

Photo by Marco Borggreve

event.title: Misery
event.description:
Nov 6, 7, 8 & 13, 14, 15, 2026      Rated M

This psychological thriller based on Stephen King’s novel Misery follows successful romance novelist Paul Sheldon, who is rescued from a car crash and wakes up captive in a secluded home owned by his self-identified “number one fan,” Annie Wilkes. While Paul is convalescing, Annie reads the manuscript of his latest book and becomes enraged when she discovers the author has killed off her favorite character, Misery Chastain. Annie forces Paul to write a new Misery novel and he quickly realizes Annie has no intention of letting him go. The irate Annie has Paul writing as if his life depends on it – and it does.

event.title: Disney’s Frozen
event.description:
Dec 11, 12, 13 & 17, 18, 19, 20, 2026      Rated PG

In the beautiful mountainous kingdom of Arendelle, Princesses Anna and Elsa grow up sheltered inside their castle, isolated from the world and increasingly distant from each other. When Elsa is crowned queen, the magical powers she’s desperately tried to conceal from her sister take control, and she flees into the mountains. As a ferocious winter descends on Arendelle, Anna sets off on an epic journey to find Elsa and bring her home – with the help of hardworking ice harvester Kristoff, his loyal reindeer Sven, and a happy-go-lucky snowman named Olaf.
Full of magic, humor, and a stunning musical score, Frozen is a powerful tale of sisterhood, acceptance, and finding the real meaning of true love.

event.title: Trolls Jr.
event.description:
January 15-24, 2027     Rated PG

Trolls JR. is based on the irreverent DreamWorks Animation movie franchise and features a colorful, wondrous world populated by hilariously unforgettable characters. The show follows the overly optimistic Trolls, constantly with a song on their lips, and the comically pessimistic Bergens, who are only happy when they have Trolls in their stomach.

The Troll thespians in Poppy’s company live by their motto: the show must go on. But when a tyrannical foreign emissary arrives in Bergenland, expectations are raised, forcing the Trolls to totally rework their show or risk being served up in the name of diplomacy by a Chef rehired and out for revenge.

 

If you would like to book a slot for one of our field trip matinees, please contact Autumn (autumnmlct@gmail.com).

event.title: Finding Neverland
event.description:
Feb 19, 20, 21 & 25, 26, 27, 28, 2027   Rated PG

J.M. Barrie, a struggling playwright, encounters a widowed mother, Sylvia Llewelyn Davies and her four sons in Kensington Park. As Barrie befriends the family, he is inspired by their adventures, particularly Peter, who is reluctant to play due to his grief. Barrie helps him to learn to play again and becomes inspired to create a new art form: children’s theatre. But who will pay to see a play about children? Who will play these characters? And how will they make Peter Pan fly?

event.title: A Gentleman’s Guide to Love and Murder
event.description:
Apr 9, 10, 11 & 16, 17, 18, 2027 Rated PG

When the low-born Monty Navarro finds out that he’s eighth in line for an earldom in the lofty D’Ysquith family, he figures his chances of outliving his predecessors are slight and sets off down a far more ghoulish path. Can he knock off his unsuspecting relatives without being caught and become the ninth Earl of Highhurst? And what of love? Because murder isn’t the only thing on Monty’s mind….

A Gentleman’s Guide to Love and Murder is a murderous romp filled with unforgettable music, non-stop laughs and a scene-stealing role for one actor playing all eight of the doomed heirs who meet their ends in the most creative and side-splitting ways. This is a must-produce for any theatre looking for a truly original and fresh new comedy that will delight audiences and leave them begging for more.

event.title: Disney’s The Little Mermaid
event.description:
July 16, 17, 18 & 22, 23, 24, 25, 2027       Rated G

Based on one of Hans Christian Andersen’s most beloved stories and the classic animated film, Disney’s The Little Mermaid is a hauntingly beautiful love story for the ages. With music by eight-time Academy Award winner, Alan Menken, lyrics by Howard Ashman and Glenn Slater and a compelling book by Doug Wright, this fishy fable will capture your heart with its irresistible songs, including “Under the Sea,” “Kiss the Girl” and “Part of Your World.”

Ariel, King Triton’s youngest daughter, wishes to pursue the human Prince Eric in the world above, bargaining with the evil sea witch, Ursula, to trade her tail for legs. But the bargain is not what it seems, and Ariel needs the help of her colorful friends, Flounder the fish, Scuttle the seagull and Sebastian the crab to restore order under the sea.

event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description:
“Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.”

This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class.

Topics include:

  • Gesture drawing fundamentals

  • Building the figure with essential forms

  • Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective

We invite all Alliance member artists to submit one original work inspired by the theme “Passage” for exhibition in the main gallery during October 2026. Call Details: Passage – Call Prospectus

 

_____________________________________________________________

Foulds Theater Gallery

Time no Time
by Dahye Kim

Ambiguous, intangible, and in flux, Dahye Kim’s installation explores time and memory as processes of becoming, dissolving, and re-emerging. Time no Time, her second solo exhibition in Florida, reflects on a reality increasingly mediated and reduced through technology and the online world. Drawn from photographs taken during her travels and thoughts developed over the past six years across diverse natural landscapes in the United States, the exhibition examines shifting perceptions of presence, memory, and temporality in digital space.

As a conceptual digital media artist, Kim creates immersive environments using video, photography, internet, coding, light, and sound. Her practice investigates the intersections of time, memory, environment, and scientific ideas through technologically mediated experiences. In this exhibition, reflective screens function as temporal mirrors in which past, present, and future collapse into a continuous surface.

Transforming the gallery into a fluid and shifting environment, Kim blurs the boundaries between material and immaterial, presence and illusion, and the natural and artificial. Minimal gestures—subtle color transitions, horizon-like lines, and shifting light—evoke unstable landscapes suspended between physical and virtual space. Her work gestures toward the evolving condition of the internet, where time fragments, loops, and becomes increasingly abstract. Through minimal digital interventions, Kim invites viewers to experience time not as linear, but as something sensed, elusive, and constantly unfolding.

More on the artist: dahyekim.com

 

_____________________________________________________________

Member Gallery

Selected Works by Marian Fuller

Marian Fuller’s mixed-media exhibition focuses on the beauty hidden within everyday life by transforming found and recycled materials into richly textured works that invite the viewer into a state of discovery. Inspired by neighborhood walks, international travel, thrift stores, and overlooked objects, she creates compositions that encourage viewers to look beyond the familiar and uncover unexpected meaning in ordinary things.

Working with handmade paper, reclaimed materials, shredded credit cards, and other found objects, Fuller embraces experimentation and sustainability, allowing each piece to tell its own story through texture and layered details. Visitors are encouraged to experience the work up close, exploring the materials and subtle surprises woven throughout the collection while discovering the joy and adventure that define her creative process.

Through guided exercises and personalized instruction, students will build confidence while developing essential drawing techniques, including observation, proportion, composition, value, and line quality. Working from a variety of subjects—including still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin drawing what is actually in front of you. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation of accurate, expressive, and confident drawing.

By the end of the seven weeks, you’ll have a stronger understanding of the fundamentals, improved observational skills, and the confidence to continue your artistic journey with a fresh perspective.

  • 2 White charcoal pencils OR White Compressed Charcoal
  • Pencil sharpener
  • Kneaded eraser

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet
event.description:
In this fun and relaxed four-week series, you’ll discover the building blocks of crochet while creating a beginner-friendly fall pumpkin. This class is designed for anyone who has wanted to learn to crochet, no prior experience required.

We’ll begin with the fundamentals, including yarn and hook basics, how to hold your materials, tension control, and the essential crochet techniques you’ll need to get started. You’ll learn how to create a slip knot and chain before progressing to basic crochet stitches as we work through the project together.

Each session we’ll build on the previous weeks, giving you plenty of time to practice, ask questions, and receive hands on guidance along the way. By the end of the series, you’ll have completed your fall pumpkin and gained a foundation of skills you can continue to build on as you explore crochet on your own.

Supplies needed:

  • 5mm or 5.5mm crochet hook
  • Medium weight acrylic yarn
    • Body: orange, rust, cream, and other lighter fall themed colors (pick one)
    • Stem: brown and green (pick one)

event.title: Drop In with Terry Lynn (All Levels)
event.description:
Interested in taking a class with beloved Instructor Terry Lynn, but not sure you can make all the sessions? Wanting to try painting, but a little worried the class might be “over your head”? Then this is your big opportunity! Drop in and try one of Terry Lynn’s painting classes – Painting with Terry Lynn AM, Painting with Terry Lynn PM or Painting Studio with Terry Lynn – whichever time and whatever Tuesday works best for you!

Students have the choice to bring in a painting they’ve been working on. Or they can take a color class, drawing class or choose something from the instructor’s materials.

Unlock your creativity in this engaging weekly painting class with beloved artist and instructor, Terry Lynn Spry! Designed for all skill levels—from beginners to seasoned professionals—this class allows students to work at their own pace with their preferred subject and medium.

event.description:
Strum, sing, and connect through music in this fun, welcoming group ukulele class for players of all levels. Whether you’re picking up an instrument for the first time or returning after a break, Amy Noel Walters will guide you through essential rhythm, chords, and technique in a way that’s supportive, creative, and confidence-building.

Unwind and unlock your inner artist with Zentangle—a simple, meditative method of drawing beautiful patterns one step at a time. Perfect for beginners, this class starts with the foundational techniques and gradually builds your confidence and creativity. Each week, you’ll create unique seasonal artworks that reflect the time of year, combining relaxation with artistic expression. No prior experience needed—just a willingness to explore, create, and enjoy the process!

event.description:
“Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.”

This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class.

Topics include:

  • Gesture drawing fundamentals

  • Building the figure with essential forms

  • Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective

  • Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution

  • Differentiating core and cast shadows

  • Sighting techniques and simplified anatomy

event.description:
Experience the spirit and rhythm of the Pacific Islands in Hula with Marliss! This dynamic class introduces students to the traditional styles of Hawaiian, Tahitian, Māori, and Samoan dance. Throughout the year, students will have the opportunity to showcase their skills and celebrate Polynesian culture at 3-4 community performances. Costumes are required for performances and are provided at a minimal cost.

Come dance, learn, and connect with the rich traditions of Polynesia in a fun and supportive environment!

event.title: He Said, She Said: Writing Better Dialogue
event.description:
Bad dialog is one of the surest signs of an amateur writer. In this course taught by award-winning novelist Roberto Calas, you’ll learn the subtle secrets of making the spoken word sing. Or written words that are spoken, sing. You get the point. Either way, readers will sing your praises with these helpful tips on dialog.

We’ll take a deep dive into the world of character speech, covering a comprehensive array of categories including:

  • Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic
  • High Tension vs. Low Tension
  • What lies beneath – Underspeak
  • Characterization Through Dialog
  • Slang and Jargon
  • Expressive Lengthening
  • Keep or Cut
  • Dialog Tags

(Optional) Bring five pages of a work in progress (containing dialog) for more personalized recommendations.

event.title: Mend & Make New
event.description: Mend & Make New is a six‑week creative repair course that teaches students how to refresh, reinforce, and reimagine their clothing using both subtle and expressive techniques. Through invisible mending, visible patchwork, embroidery, darning, and hybrid redesign, students learn how to assess damage, choose the right materials, and build repairs that are both durable and personal. The class blends practical skill‑building with organic, discovery‑based learning while encouraging students to explore materials, experiment with stitches, and find their own style of repair. By the end of the series, each student completes a final project that combines multiple techniques and celebrates the character of well‑loved garments.

event.title: Life Drawing Lounge
event.description:
Now on Wednesday evenings 6-9pm AND Sunday afternoons 1-4pm!

Drop in, settle in, and draw! Life Drawing Lounge is a relaxed, non-instructed life drawing session featuring a nude model in one extended pose. Designed for artists of all levels with some basic life drawing experience, this is an opportunity to practice, experiment, and develop your skills in a casual, welcoming environment.

Enjoy music, light conversation, and the freedom to work at your own pace. Artists are encouraged to bring and use the medium of their choice.

$20 at the door

event.title: Picture Perfect: Exploring Photo Editing Techniques
event.description:
You already take great photos with your camera or cell phone, but what happens after you press the shutter?

With endless tutorials, YouTube videos, and AI tools at our fingertips, learning photo editing has never been more accessible. But there’s still tremendous value in sitting down with an experienced photographer who can help you understand not just how to edit, but why certain techniques work.

Led by digital lab instructor and photographer Robert Ahrens, this session explores the evolving world of digital photo editing, from traditional editing techniques to the newest AI-powered tools found in today’s software and online platforms. Learn how to improve your images, streamline your editing workflow, and make thoughtful creative choices rather than simply relying on automatic corrections.

We’ll also look at what you can do before you even press the shutter to give yourself a better image to work with later. Whether you’re photographing Florida wildlife, beaches, architecture, or our spectacular sunrises and sunsets, understanding the fundamentals of exposure, composition, resolution, and file quality can make a significant difference in your final results.

This class is designed for everyone from the weekend photographer looking to sharpen their skills to semi-professional photographers and local realtors who want to create more polished, compelling images for their work.

The Quill at Alliance for the Arts is a writers group with the goal of building a stronger creative writing community in Southwest Florida. We are, primarily, a fiction critique group, but The Quill is also a place to practice your craft, learn new skills, network with other writers, and discuss all writing-related matters. The moderator–historical-fantasy author Roberto Calas–will maintain a safe, supportive space for all participants. All skill levels and genres are welcome.

Meeting the first  and third Thursdays from 6:30 – 9pm of every month

event.description:
Step into a creative space where experimentation is encouraged and there’s no single “right” way to make art. In this ongoing studio-style class, teens will explore a wide range of materials and techniques while building confidence in their artistic voice.

Each week introduces a new theme, artist, or source of inspiration, paired with guided mini-lessons that spark ideas and expand creative skills. Students will have the freedom to explore painting, drawing, mixed media, and more—while also continuing to develop personal projects over time.

This class balances structure with creative freedom, helping teens strengthen foundational skills, discover new mediums, and grow as artists in a supportive, inspiring environment. Single sessions available for $25/member, attend one session, or all 5!

event.title: Sip and Create: Fall Flower Fun
event.description:
Celebrate the beauty of autumn by creating a one-of-a-kind floral vase using the timeless art of decoupage. In this relaxing, hands-on workshop, participants will embellish a glass vase with delicate pressed flowers, transforming it into a beautiful piece of functional art. As you slow down, create, and enjoy the process, you’ll learn simple decoupage techniques that are easy to recreate at home.

Perfect for displaying fresh fall blooms or as a thoughtful handmade gift, your finished vase will bring warmth and beauty to your home throughout the season. All supplies are provided, including the vase, pressed flowers, decoupage materials, and finishing supplies. Each participant will leave with a completed keepsake vase and the satisfaction of creating something both beautiful and meaningful.

event.title: Alliance Morning Market
event.description:
The Alliance for the Arts has reimagined its community market experience with the launch of the Alliance Morning Artisan Market, a new monthly event held on the third Saturday of each month from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. The shift moves the Alliance’s former Wednesday night market to a vibrant Saturday morning gathering designed to bring families, artists, and the community together for a full day of creativity and connection.

The first Alliance Morning Market will take place Saturday, Feb. 21, 2026, on the Alliance’s 10-acre campus at 10091 McGregor Blvd. The market will feature a curated mix of artisans and vendors, local artists, and live entertainment, creating a welcoming, festival-style atmosphere for all ages.

By moving the market to Saturdays, the Alliance is aligning it with two popular free programs already offered on campus: Free Family ArtLabs, held from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., and Reel Families, Free Family Movie Screenings, beginning at noon. Together, these programs create a seamless day of activities centered on creativity, community, and family-friendly fun.

“The Alliance Morning Market allows us to bring together so many of the things our community loves, local artists, creative experiences for kids, live entertainment, and time spent together,” said Alliance representative and organizer, Cat Flo. “It’s more than a market; it’s a full morning and afternoon of connection.”

Admission to the Alliance Morning Market and all accompanying activities is free. While gallery admission is always free, a $5 suggested donation helps support the Alliance’s mission to keep arts programming accessible and affordable.

Event: Alliance Morning Market, Indoors & Outdoors

Date: Every Third Saturday  Time: 9am–1pm

Includes: Local Vendors | Live Entertainment | Family ArtLab |  Free Family Movie

For more information about the Alliance Morning Market or other Alliance programs, visit ArtInLee.org or call 239-939-2787. For vending opportunities contact Cat@artinlee.org.

event.description:

Inspired by the beautifully hand-painted metal trays of Zhostovo painting, students will learn the signature “Russian Stroke” method used to create lush, dimensional floral designs set against rich, dark backgrounds.

Throughout the series, you’ll build skills step by step — practicing brush control, double-loading techniques, blending, highlights, and shadow work — before applying your knowledge to design and completing your own decorative tray. We’ll explore traditional compositions, color harmony, and the bold contrast that makes this style so striking.

Perfect for beginners ready to learn foundational stroke work as well as experienced painters wanting to expand their decorative painting repertoire. By the end of the course, you’ll leave with a beautifully painted tray and the confidence to continue exploring this timeless folk art tradition.

event.title: Just Make
event.description:
You already know how to do this.

You’ve been making marks your whole life. In the margins of notebooks. On napkins. On the back of envelopes while you were thinking about something else entirely.

That impulse — the one that moves the pen before you decide to — is the most honest creative act you have. It’s also the one most people spend their entire lives dismissing.

Just Make is a one-day mixed-media workshop that gives that impulse a canvas, some paint, a pair of scissors, and permission.

We start fast. Marks get made before the critic wakes up. Paper gets torn. Things get glued in places that don’t make sense yet. Decisions happen at the speed of instinct — which is exactly the right speed for this.

Then something shifts.

The eye takes over. Composition emerges. You slow down and discover you’ve already made something worth finishing. The pieces were always going to go where they went.

You’ll leave with finished work on two surfaces — a canvas and a glass-mounted piece called a Slide — and the unsettling realization that you could have been doing this all along.

All primary materials provided. No experience necessary. No plan required.

Just show up.

Just make.

event.title: Step By Step Batik: Sunflower
event.description:
Explore the Art of Wax and Watercolor with a Fabric-Like Finish

If you’re looking for a unique and immersive art experience, this full-day workshop is not to be missed. Inspired by the traditional Indonesian technique of Batik, you’ll create a stunning layered painting using melted wax, watercolor, and Ginwashi rice paper — known for its beautiful translucent texture.

Guided by your instructor, you’ll work with multiple templates and learn how to build up color and design using wax-resist methods. The result is a one-of-a-kind painting with the look and feel of delicate, hand-dyed fabric. This class is perfect for beginners and seasoned artists alike who are eager to try something new.

A break will be taken for lunch on your own. Limited to just 6 participants to ensure plenty of individual instruction.


All supplies are provided

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet
event.description:
In this fun and relaxed four-week series, you’ll discover the building blocks of crochet while creating a beginner-friendly fall pumpkin. This class is designed for anyone who has wanted to learn to crochet, no prior experience required.

We’ll begin with the fundamentals, including yarn and hook basics, how to hold your materials, tension control, and the essential crochet techniques you’ll need to get started. You’ll learn how to create a slip knot and chain before progressing to basic crochet stitches as we work through the project together.

Each session we’ll build on the previous weeks, giving you plenty of time to practice, ask questions, and receive hands on guidance along the way. By the end of the series, you’ll have completed your fall pumpkin and gained a foundation of skills you can continue to build on as you explore crochet on your own.

Supplies needed:

  • 5mm or 5.5mm crochet hook
  • Medium weight acrylic yarn
    • Body: orange, rust, cream, and other lighter fall themed colors (pick one)
    • Stem: brown and green (pick one)

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Prometheus Bound-Waldorf Inspired Story Class (Ages 9-11)
event.description:
In Prometheus Bound, students encounter the story of Prometheus and Epimetheus through oral narration, chalkboard drawing, discussion, and the creation of their own Main Lesson Books.
Their Main Lesson Books will be created from their own understanding and interpretation of the story rather than by simply copying the teacher’s work. Through writing, drawing, and bookmaking, students will develop a personal record of the myth while engaging its imagery, characters, and ideas in a distinctly Waldorf-inspired way.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Wise Humans (Ages 9-11)
event.description:
A Waldorf-Inspired Philosophy II Class

Building on the philosophical exploration begun in Philosophy I, Wise Humans takes students further into the strange problems, thought experiments, paradoxes, and ideas philosophers have used to investigate reality, knowledge, reason, and the human experience. Through storytelling, conversation, philosophical puzzles, and Waldorf-inspired Main Lesson Book work, students will encounter problems designed not simply to be solved, but to complicate what initially seems obvious. Students will consider questions of stability and change, the limits of knowledge, consciousness and perception, rational choice, time, meaning, and the peculiar difficulties that arise when apparently reasonable ideas collide.
The class emphasizes philosophical exploration rather than arriving at prescribed conclusions. Students will practice following an argument, noticing assumptions, considering competing possibilities, and becoming comfortable with questions that remain genuinely unsettled.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: What Is…Art? (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
Rather than beginning with definitions, students will encounter objects, ideas, provocations, and philosophical problems that complicate the boundary between art and everything else.
The goal of the class is to not create art. Instead, students will attempt to understand art by testing its boundaries—asking what can be removed, changed, ignored, or rejected before something stops being art at all.

There may not be an answer. That’s the point.

 

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Wisdom Without the Hemlock-Arts/Philosophy Class II (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
Wisdom without the Hemlock is a four-week arts and philosophy workshop built around the spirit of Socratic inquiry. Through Socrates, the Sophists, the Presocratics, dialogue, and philosophical problems, students will examine certainty, knowledge, and the nature of reality. Rather than memorizing a history of philosophy, students will practice questioning assumptions, following arguments, and thinking carefully, all while cultivating curiosity and wonder.

Know that you don’t know, so never stop asking.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Drop In with Terry Lynn (All Levels)
event.description:
Interested in taking a class with beloved Instructor Terry Lynn, but not sure you can make all the sessions? Wanting to try painting, but a little worried the class might be “over your head”? Then this is your big opportunity! Drop in and try one of Terry Lynn’s painting classes – Painting with Terry Lynn AM, Painting with Terry Lynn PM or Painting Studio with Terry Lynn – whichever time and whatever Tuesday works best for you!

Students have the choice to bring in a painting they’ve been working on. Or they can take a color class, drawing class or choose something from the instructor’s materials.

You may bring your own supplies (check supply list from Tuesday class) or purchase supply kit from the instructor for $20.

event.title: Contemporary Painting with Terry Lynn
event.description:
Unlock your creativity in this engaging weekly painting class with beloved artist and instructor, Terry Lynn Spry! Designed for all skill levels—from beginners to seasoned professionals—this class allows students to work at their own pace with their preferred subject and medium.

Explore a wide range of painting styles, from realism to abstract, while deepening your understanding of portraiture, color control, composition, value studies, and drawing techniques. With personalized guidance and a supportive environment, you’ll refine your skills and develop your artistic voice.

Choose the best time of day for you:

Morning- 9:30am-12:30pm

Afternoon- 1pm-4pm

Evening- 6:30pm-9pm

Times available to choose in the registration process.

  • Alizarin Crimson

  • Cadmium Red

  • Cadmium Yellow Light

  • Phthalo Blue

  • Ultramarine Blue

  • Ivory Black

  • Titanium White

Brushes:

  • Filberts (Sizes 2, 4, 6, 8)

  • Soft Synthetic Brushes

  • Container for Water (for acrylics)

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: The Tempest: An Arts Encounter with Shakespeare’s The Tempest (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
The Tempest is a four-week arts and literature class for ages 13+ centered on the journey of Prospero as he confronts power, control, forgiveness, and the question of how to act once one possesses knowledge and agency. Each class begins with discussion and clarification of the assigned portion of the play. Students will examine Prospero’s changing relationship to the island, to the people
around him, and to his own power. In the second hour, students will create a landscape painting that represents where they understand Prospero to be at that point in his journey, drawing loosely on the compositional tradition of Taoist landscape painting. Over the course of the class, the three paintings will form a visual record of Prospero’s movement through the play. In the final session, the panels will be assembled into a triptych chronicling that journey.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Group Ukulele Lessons
event.description:
Strum, sing, and connect through music in this fun, welcoming group ukulele class for players of all levels. Whether you’re picking up an instrument for the first time or returning after a break, Amy Noel Walters will guide you through essential rhythm, chords, and technique in a way that’s supportive, creative, and confidence-building.

Each class blends hands-on practice with clear, easy-to-follow instruction, helping you build a strong musical foundation while exploring songs you love. You’ll also discover simple ways to incorporate breath, mindfulness, and body awareness into your playing, making music not just something you play, but something you feel. Bring your instrument, your curiosity, and a smile because making music is better together.

What to bring: Ukulele, tuner, water, and a notebook

Supply fee of $15 due directly to the Instructor


Single-class options available during the registration process. $30/members $35/non-members

event.title: Advanced Drawing for Tweens and Teens (Ages11-16)
event.description:
Drawing by Emily, age 11

Discover the skills to draw with greater confidence and realism! If you’ve ever wanted to improve your drawing abilities, this class will teach you how to truly see your subject rather than simply draw what you think it looks like. Through a series of guided exercises, you’ll learn techniques that help train your eye to recognize proportion, shape, value, and light.

Experiment with a variety of drawing materials, including charcoal pencils, compressed charcoal, and other black-and-white media, while building your skills through a range of subjects. You’ll draw still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models, developing the ability to capture light, shadow, depth, and form with greater accuracy.

Supplies Needed: 

  • 2 Charcoal Pencils, 6B extra soft
  • 2 White charcoal pencils OR White Compressed Charcoal
  • Pencil sharpener
  • Kneaded eraser

Paper provided

event.title: Zentangle for the Seasons
event.description:
Discover the Art of Zentangle: A Creative Journey Through the Seasons
Unwind and unlock your inner artist with Zentangle—a simple, meditative method of drawing beautiful patterns one step at a time. Perfect for beginners, this class starts with the foundational techniques and gradually builds your confidence and creativity. Each week, you’ll create unique seasonal artworks that reflect the time of year, combining relaxation with artistic expression. No prior experience needed—just a willingness to explore, create, and enjoy the process!

Supplies provided for a $10 fee due directly to the Instructor

event.title: Fine Art Acrylics with Marilyn Hedlund
event.description:
Join artist Marilyn Hedlund for a dynamic, critique-based class designed to inspire artists of all levels. Each session begins and ends with lively group critiques where ideas, techniques, and feedback are shared freely in a supportive environment.

Between critiques, you’ll work at your own station and pace, developing your artwork with personalized, one-on-one guidance from Marilyn. Expect to be challenged and inspired through stimulating discussions, creative assignments, and lecture/demos on essential topics like composition, form, color, and contrast.

This is more than a class—it’s a creative community where fresh ideas, constructive critique, and artistic growth go hand in hand.

  • Various pens, pencils, charcoal, drawing tools

event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description:
“Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.”

This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class.

Topics include:

  • Gesture drawing fundamentals

  • Building the figure with essential forms

  • Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective

  • Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution

  • Differentiating core and cast shadows

  • Sighting techniques and simplified anatomy

Whether you’re just starting or refining your figure drawing skills, Francesco’s instruction will help you grow with clarity and confidence.

Supplies Needed:

* 2 Charcoal pencils 2B
* 1 White plastic eraser
* 1 Kneaded eraser
* 1 18″x 24″ Newsprint pad – 100 sheet
* Blending stumps assorted sizes 4 pc.
* No oils, solvent or fixatives are allowed in the class

event.title: Hula Dance (Ages 3-12)
event.description:
Experience the spirit and rhythm of the Pacific Islands in Hula with Marliss! This dynamic class introduces students to the traditional styles of Hawaiian, Tahitian, Māori, and Samoan dance. With a focus on both technique and cultural appreciation, students will learn the foundations of each style while mastering vibrant performance dances and songs.

Throughout the year, students will have the opportunity to showcase their skills and celebrate Polynesian culture at 3-4 community performances. Costumes are required for performances and are provided at a minimal cost.

Come dance, learn, and connect with the rich traditions of Polynesia in a fun and supportive environment!

event.title: Mend & Make New
event.description: Mend & Make New is a six‑week creative repair course that teaches students how to refresh, reinforce, and reimagine their clothing using both subtle and expressive techniques. Through invisible mending, visible patchwork, embroidery, darning, and hybrid redesign, students learn how to assess damage, choose the right materials, and build repairs that are both durable and personal. The class blends practical skill‑building with organic, discovery‑based learning while encouraging students to explore materials, experiment with stitches, and find their own style of repair. By the end of the series, each student completes a final project that combines multiple techniques and celebrates the character of well‑loved garments.

event.title: Life Drawing Lounge
event.description:
Now on Wednesday evenings 6-9pm AND Sunday afternoons 1-4pm!

Drop in, settle in, and draw! Life Drawing Lounge is a relaxed, non-instructed life drawing session featuring a nude model in one extended pose. Designed for artists of all levels with some basic life drawing experience, this is an opportunity to practice, experiment, and develop your skills in a casual, welcoming environment.

event.title: Picture Perfect: Exploring Photo Editing Techniques
event.description:
You already take great photos with your camera or cell phone, but what happens after you press the shutter?

With endless tutorials, YouTube videos, and AI tools at our fingertips, learning photo editing has never been more accessible. But there’s still tremendous value in sitting down with an experienced photographer who can help you understand not just how to edit, but why certain techniques work.

Led by digital lab instructor and photographer Robert Ahrens, this session explores the evolving world of digital photo editing, from traditional editing techniques to the newest AI-powered tools found in today’s software and online platforms. Learn how to improve your images, streamline your editing workflow, and make thoughtful creative choices rather than simply relying on automatic corrections.

We’ll also look at what you can do before you even press the shutter to give yourself a better image to work with later. Whether you’re photographing Florida wildlife, beaches, architecture, or our spectacular sunrises and sunsets, understanding the fundamentals of exposure, composition, resolution, and file quality can make a significant difference in your final results.

This class is designed for everyone from the weekend photographer looking to sharpen their skills to semi-professional photographers and local realtors who want to create more polished, compelling images for their work.

Bring your questions and curiosity and leave with new tools and techniques to take your photography to the next level.

event.title: Watercolor with Linda Benson
event.description:
Enjoy being creative with transparent watercolors. Linda Benson’s hands-on teaching technique allows you to create along with her in the classroom. Learn something new or refresh your skills. You will learn brush techniques, color theory, perspective, gradients, and composition. Each week is a new lesson complete with reference handouts. You will learn tricks that aren’t in the book and secrets for a successful painting.

  • 6 Primary transparent watercolor tubes – any Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Violet (traditional tube watercolors are transparent like Daniels, Holbein, & Windsor Newton, QoR, not opaque. Look for transparent tubes not round cakes)
  • Watercolor brushes: Round and flat assortment with 1 inch flat
  • 140 Lb. Watercolor paper or block 11×14 (Arches is good watercolor paper but Strathmore is OK if it is 140-pound stock)
  • Watercolor pallet tray with cover
  • Bring 2 water cups
  • 1 roll of paper towels
  • Small note book or mini sketch book
  • Pencils
  • Blue ballpoint pen
  • Pencil erasers
  • Carry bag
  • Pencil case
  • If you already have some supplies, bring in what you have and we will work with that. Linda will have some brushes and some supplies to share on the first day of class for beginners. Advanced students bring what you have.

event.title: Master the Comma Stroke with Pat Smelkoff
event.description:
Discover the beauty of movement and rhythm in this engaging Comma workshop. In this hands-on class, you’ll learn how to use the expressive “comma” brushstroke to build texture, depth, and flow within your artwork. This versatile technique allows you to create everything from soft florals to dynamic landscapes using simple, repeated strokes.

With step-by-step guidance, you’ll explore brush control, layering, and composition while developing a style that feels both intuitive and meditative. Perfect for all skill levels, this class offers a relaxing, process-driven approach to painting, and a fresh technique you can carry into all your future work.

All supplies provided. This is a process driven workshop; you’ll leave with knowledge about the process, not a completed painting.

event.title: Art Without Rules: Teen MultiMedia Space (Age 13-18)

Step into a creative space where experimentation is encouraged and there’s no single “right” way to make art. In this ongoing studio-style class, teens will explore a wide range of materials and techniques while building confidence in their artistic voice.

Each week introduces a new theme, artist, or source of inspiration, paired with guided mini-lessons that spark ideas and expand creative skills. Students will have the freedom to explore painting, drawing, mixed media, and more—while also continuing to develop personal projects over time.

This class balances structure with creative freedom, helping teens strengthen foundational skills, discover new mediums, and grow as artists in a supportive, inspiring environment. Single sessions available for $25/member, attend one session, or all 5!

event.title: Oil Painting Basics
event.description:
Build confidence and develop your painting skills in this comprehensive 7-week oil painting course designed for both beginners and experienced artists. Whether you’re picking up a brush for the first time or looking to strengthen your technique, this class offers personalized instruction and guided exercises that will help you grow as a painter.

Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings.

By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently.

For the first 2 classes, we will be limiting our palette to black and white.

event.title: Drawing Fundamentals (Ages 16+)
event.description:

Whether you’re a complete beginner who thinks you can’t draw or an experienced artist looking to refresh your skills and see your work in a new way, this class offers a supportive and engaging environment to grow.

Through guided exercises and personalized instruction, students will build confidence while developing essential drawing techniques, including observation, proportion, composition, value, and line quality. Working from a variety of subjects—including still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin drawing what is actually in front of you. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation of accurate, expressive, and confident drawing.

By the end of the seven weeks, you’ll have a stronger understanding of the fundamentals, improved observational skills, and the confidence to continue your artistic journey with a fresh perspective.

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet

event.description:

Their Main Lesson Books will be created from their own understanding and interpretation of the story rather than by simply copying the teacher’s work. Through writing, drawing, and bookmaking, students will develop a personal record of the myth while engaging its imagery, characters, and ideas in a distinctly Waldorf-inspired way.
